sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for Ocala
sections.html:
Ocala sits in Marion County, so the county appraiser sets its values and the county collector mails the bills. The City of Ocala, the county commission and the school board are among the bodies that set millage.

The appraiser's office is at 501 SE 25th Avenue in Ocala. Walk-ins are welcome, and you can also make an appointment. The website offers a homestead e-file, a tax estimator, a mortgage estimate letter, an address change request and links to the TRIM notice and the value adjustment board.

Another Marion County exists in Texas with its own tax office, so make sure you are on the Florida sites when you look up a parcel.

Ocala had 71,753 residents in the 2025 estimate, 12.7 percent more than the 2020 base, across 47.26 square miles. The median owner-occupied value is $241,400 and median gross rent is $1,359. Only 52.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rental parcels are common. Rented homes cannot hold a homestead exemption, so a landlord selling an Ocala rental should expect the buyer's bill to follow the non-homestead rules.

Median owner costs are $1,598 a month with a mortgage and $573 without one, a gap worth showing a buyer who has never owned.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
The appraiser multiplies value after exemptions by the millage the taxing bodies set, then certifies the roll for collection. The calendar below follows the state schedule.

Ocala property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set
March 1Exemption applications close
AugustTRIM notice mails; 25 days to petition on value, 30 days to contest a denied exemption
NovemberBills mail; 4 percent discount
March 31Deferral applications due with Form DR-570
April 1Unpaid bills turn delinquent

The appraiser's estimator is a good starting point for a buyer. A buyer's value is reset after a sale, so a seller's old bill will not match it.

Most chores can be finished without a trip to the office. The appraiser's home page links to these tools:

  • Property search, a map tool and a sales search for checking what nearby parcels went for.
  • A homestead exemption e-file and a property tax estimator.
  • A mortgage estimate letter, which lenders and buyers sometimes request.
  • A mailing address change request, useful when you move out before the sale closes.
  • A form to report property damage, and a separate link to report homestead fraud.
  • Pages for tangible personal property: an e-filed return, an extension request and forms.

Before you list an Ocala home, run the sales search for your street and print the results. Comparable sales are the best answer to a buyer who asks why your price differs from the assessed value. The office also posts important dates, a taxpayer's bill of rights and frequently asked questions.

sections.h2: Selling an Ocala rental or an inherited house
sections.html:
With so many units not owner-occupied, many Ocala sellers are investors or heirs, not homestead owners. Their parcels fall under the 10 percent yearly cap for non-homestead property, which ends with the sale.

Heirs face a few extra steps. Stamp tax does not apply to a personal representative's deed under a probated will, though estate planning transfers have no general exemption. No Florida estate tax return is due for deaths after 2004.

  • Summary administration fits a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less, or a death more than two years back.

Seniors with limited income may defer part of a homestead bill. Ask the tax collector how a deferral affects a sale before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: What to do before you accept an offer
sections.html:
Start with the parcel record on the appraiser's site and check the owner name, mailing address and exemptions on the roll. A wrong name or address delays notices, and a leftover exemption on a house that has been rented will draw questions from the buyer's lender.

Next, confirm with the tax collector that every year is paid. Florida bills run on the calendar year, so a house that sells in the summer has a current-year bill that has not been mailed, and the title company will estimate it. If the house was ever rented furnished, furniture and equipment left in the unit are taxed as tangible personal property, and a return is due by April 1.

  • Ask the title company for a tax proration worksheet early.
  • Gather any denial letters or value notices still in dispute.
  • Tell the buyer which taxing bodies appear on the bill, including the City of Ocala.

A 4 percent cut comes off November payments, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. An owner who gets no bill is still the one who must find out the amount and pay before April 1.

Owners who cannot pay at once can ask the collector about installments, applied for by May 1, or a partial payment before delinquency. Limited-income seniors may defer part of a homestead bill with Form DR-570 by March 31.

To qualify for the exemption of up to $50,000, the house must be your permanent residence on January 1, and the application is due March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value was capped at 2.7 percent for 2026.

A sale resets the next assessment to just value, with exceptions for spouse transfers and certain transfers on death. An owner buying again in Florida can ask the appraiser about carrying savings to the new home through portability.

sections.h2: What happens at an Ocala closing
sections.html:
The title company confirms the payoff figures, prorates the current year's tax between you and the buyer, and collects your signature on the deed. The clerk then records it. Plan to review the settlement statement a day ahead so you can ask about any tax line you do not recognize.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which shortens the calendar. The tax and title work stays the same: open balances are paid from your proceeds and recorded liens are released before the buyer takes title.

sections.h2: Deed taxes, fees and back taxes
sections.html:
A deed for an Ocala property is taxed at the statewide 70 cents per $100 of consideration (section 201.02). Everyone on the deed stays liable, and the clerk takes payment. Recording starts at $5.00 for the opening page under section 28.24.

  • Warranty, special warranty and quit claim deeds are taxable.
  • Certain spousal and divorce deeds for the marital home are exempt.

Back taxes lead to certificates sold by June 1 and, later, a possible deed sale. Clear the account with the collector before listing, and ask your title company to pull the payoff so the closing figures are firm.

faqs.q: Which county taxes a home in Ocala?
faqs.a: Marion County, Florida. The county's appraiser values the home and its collector bills it, using millage from several bodies that includes the City of Ocala.

faqs.q: What is Ocala's median home value?
faqs.a: $241,400. Median rent is $1,359, and 52.1 percent of units have owners living in them.

faqs.q: Where can an Ocala owner visit the appraiser?
faqs.a: At 501 SE 25th Avenue in Ocala. Walk-ins and appointments are both welcome, and the phone number is (352) 368-8300.

faqs.q: Can an Ocala rental property have homestead?
faqs.a: No. Homestead is lost if the unit is rented, so a rental is assessed without the exemption and the owner's cap does not transfer to a buyer.

faqs.q: Is the Ocala tax bill reset when the house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of title sends the next assessment to just value, so a buyer cannot count on the seller's bill.
